utterances.text: Your Honour, we will use this document, with your permission, for the purposes of impeachment. And we understand that will be the purpose through the remainder of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Do you have any submissions on the other points that are raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This particular document, 65 ter 2022, was disclosed to the Defence on the 2nd of February, 2007, via CD-ROM. So that's three years ago, Your Honour. We are -- again, we are -- seek to use this document to challenge the witness's testimony that the Drina Plan was not an authentic plan. That is the purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have already told me that you want to impeach. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Right. And, again, the Prosecution was not aware of the Defence position on this matter until Wednesday afternoon, and that's why we feel that it would be in the interests of justice to use this document for this purpose at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What was the mode of disclosure?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: CD-ROM, Your Honour. That's been the mode of disclosure throughout this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There is an issue raised about the languages known to counsel and the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We would have -- this document, originally, is in B/C/S, Your Honour, and that would have been the language that it was disclosed in. Before any translation, it was disclosed in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Are you done?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have but one remark, understanding that the Prosecution seeks to introduce this document for the sole purpose of impeachment and none other, and the argument being, as I understand, that they seek to use this document to challenge the witness's testimony the Drina Plan was not an authentic plan, I have only one concern, which is: At the time the Drina Plan was tendered by the Prosecution, through Mr. Treanor, the Prosecution indicated --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel speak close to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do apologise. The Prosecution indicated, beginning at page 1200, the question from Ms. Sutherland: "Q. Mr. Treanor, did the FRY continue to provide military assistance to the Bosnian Serbs? "A. Yes. "Q. Have you seen any new documents that reflect the ultimate goal of the FRY leadership? "A. Yes. "Q. Did General Perisic have knowledge of this goal? "A. Yes." After which point in time we went into private session, because at that point in time the Drina Plan was a protected document, and the document that was introduced was the Drina Plan. Thereafter, the next day, subsequent parts of the Drina Plan were once again introduced. I understand what the Prosecution's position is here. However, I believe, as I indicated earlier, that this is something that should have been introduced in their case in chief. However, having heard the arguments made by Mr. Saxon, I believe that he probably has met the threshold with regard to the issue of impeachment. So I've just done something that I think on occasion you object to, Your Honour, which is I've answered a question in a rather long fashion. I believe that Mr. Saxon has obtained --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Shall I finish it for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- the threshold of -- for his purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are -- you are withdrawing the objection at this stage; is that the short answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be the short answer, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would you call in the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could Mr. Simic please return. While we're waiting for the witness to be brought in, could the Drina binder be brought to his desk, please. It's a particular binder marked "Drina number 1." I'm sorry, I can't hear you, sir. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If you can just wait for the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry it took long, but it's resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's resolved, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon, you may -- the Prosecution may use Exhibit 2022 -- 65 ter 2022 to question the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And if we could turn to tab 9 in that binder, please, and if we could call up 65 ter -- we've already called it up. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, if you look at your version of the document, we'll see that it says: "People's Defence, State Secret, Drina, Attachment 10, Copy 2." Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it's an order for engineering support of the Republika Srpska Army. And there is a stamp from the Army of Republika Srpska Main Staff at the bottom of the first page. And as you go to the last page, we'll see that this is stamped again and signed by General Mladic. Can we agree with that so far?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This kind of order for engineering support, again, is this the kind of order you would expect to see in a directive like the Drina Plan?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a -- this is an attachment or an appendix about engineering support from the Drina Plan, and it's from the Main Staff of the VRS. And such documents can be found in any plan of use, so that the Main Staff, in their plan, also had this appendix.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, and I hope I'm following the correct procedural wavelength, I would seek to tender this document for the purposes that we talked about before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2893. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yesterday, in response to one of my questions, General, you said that: "Had the Drina Plan been a complete plan of use and had extracts been provided to the Main Staffs, they would have to elaborate plans for their own units, including a more detailed operationalisation in terms of carrying out the said tasks." That's at page 10148 of the transcript, lines 14 to 17. If you go, General, to what is tab 10 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could bring up on e-court what is Exhibit P1562, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You'll see, General, that this is a document from the Command of the 1st Krajina Corps that was submitted -- it was a list of 1st Krajina Corps documents submitted to the General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. At the top right-hand corner, it says: "National Defence, State Secret, Drina R, Copy 1." And then in the list itself we see a list of 14 documents, going from: Order for defence attack operation; decision for defence attack operation map; order for intelligence security, intelligence security plan; all the way down to number 14, which is "Logistical support." Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Entirely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see at the bottom -- first of all, we see a stamp of the 1st Krajina Corps, isn't that right, of the Command of the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dated the 29th of January, 1994. You see it was received by a person whose name has not been translated in English, but I'm wondering if you can read it in your language. Does that say "R. Miletic," if you can read it, or "Neletic"? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it looks like, "Miletic."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this would be an example, this particular list of documents from the 1st Krajina Corps, this would be an example of the, to use your term, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The operationalisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I better find it, because it's late on Friday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This would be an example, I think, if you'll agree with me, of the more detailed operationalisation from the units below the Main Staff, in terms of carrying out the said tasks; would that be right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, will you allow me a few sentences in order to explain this?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. This kind of list of documents, indicating --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, the interpreters ask that you please repeat your answer slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. It seems that everybody's affected by the fact that it's Friday. When I was talking about -- about the Drina Directive, signed by the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, this directive had to be operationalised and extracted therefrom, submitted to the commands of lower units, each army to their respective units. We see here the mention of an order for defence. The Main Staff would have a directive on this. Another key element on the plan of use is a decision, a decision that has to be approved by the president of the FRY, because this decision affects the operationalisation of the texts of the directive, and that applied to everything else. However, we don't see that as being elaborated at the level of the General Staff. However, the only thing that exists is the text of the directive that was signed at the strategic global level, and for those on the ground who have to carry it out, this does not mean a lot. Here, the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps handed over these documents to someone who succeeded him, who received the plan of use, because that is how the record of hand-over of these documents is usually made. I hope I've been clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You have been clear. But with the greatest respect, you haven't answered the question that I asked you. Let me just repeat it again briefly. My question was simply: Was this document that we've just looked at from the 1st Krajina Corps Command, would that be an example of the more -- what you referred to yesterday, the more detailed operationalisation from the units below the Main Staff? That was my question. Just -- if you can say, Yes, or, No, or --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For my own refreshment of my memory, by the way, to which army does the 1st Krajina Corps belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It belonged to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. Your Honours, everything that we are discussing concerning the Drina Plan relates to the plan of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, for which I was not in charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand. But it is also interacting with the VJ, isn't it? You may proceed, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, with this -- excuse me. I just may have one follow-up question, if you will allow me to look at the transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I just want to clarify your response to Judge Moloto's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO ASKED YOU
utterances.text: "To which army does the 1st Krajina Corps belong?" And you responded: "It belonged to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska." Just so everything is clear, are you saying that the corps, the Krajina Corps, was an organisational unit of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was subordinated to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, just like the commander of the 1st Army was subordinate to the Chief of General Staff of the VJ. This is the standard chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, just before we break, I'm now at a point where I believe some further discussion on the same legal issue will be necessary, but it involves a group of documents. So I think it only needs to be one discussion for a few minutes, and so it may be best, with Your Honour's leave, that, when we come back, that the witness remain in the waiting room for a few moments while we deal with this matter once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we come back to the issue of fresh evidence. The last document that you saw was Prosecution Exhibit P1562, which was a list of 1st Krajina Corps documents. P1562 was the first document in a group of documents that was obtained by the Office of the Prosecutor from the Government of Republika Srpska. Only P1562 was placed on the Prosecution's 65 ter list and tendered into evidence. What the Prosecution seeks leave of the Trial Chamber to do is to -- it has the documents that were mentioned on this list, that is, P1562, which it didn't place on its 65 ter list at that time. All of these documents were disclosed to the Defence on the 2nd of February, 2007, more than three years ago. And like the last document, Your Honour, we seek the Chamber's leave to use this series of documents from the 1st Krajina Corps for purposes of impeachment of the witness. And I'm referring to this series of documents, because it seems -- I think it's -- I think, with the Chamber's leave, rather than dealing with each document separately, this can be the subject of a single discussion and single decision. And if you allow me to go on, Your Honours, the Prosecution also obtained documents related to the Drina Plan from the Drina Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might interject, since I think we're going into a new subject, new documents. Could you please identify for us specifically which of the documents you're referring to in that first grouping, just so that when we're dealing with this, we can deal with this in a discreet fashion, because they may be treated differently by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we have P1562 back on the monitor, please. Do you see the list, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I do. My --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Those are the documents that the Prosecution says it seeks leave to tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand. What I'm asking for is these -- I have a series of documents that were presented to us, in the neighbourhood of some approximately 200 -- 200-plus documents that the Prosecution intends on using for purposes of cross-examination. Of those documents, a certain number of those documents are designated XN, XN-1, XN-2, XN-3. All I'm asking for is to know which XN numbers they are so that I can correlate Mr. Saxon's position with what he's representing. It's not that I disbelieve him. It's just that I want to be organised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to help, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. And if we just stick with the Krajina Corps documents for now, that would be what has been up-loaded on e-court from XN-144 through XN-155. And these are the documents that are on the list that is P1562, with one exception, and that is the second item on the list, which is a map. That, we do not have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Therein lies my initial dilemma, because I have different numbers. So I'm not sure that I'm following what you've suggested. I have as your last document XN-143 being an SRK Drina Plan. I'm just trying to be with you. That's not what you've talked about thus far. I have 144 as being a document concerning some criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That is a surprise to me, quite frankly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Maybe I've done something wrong, so let me just double --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Maybe I've done something wrong, so let me check, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In fact, XN-143 would not be part of the list, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I was only using that for reference to put us into co-ordination. Let me just co-ordinate here. Why don't you proceed, then, because I'll be able to figure out where the difficulty lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think, for the sake of simplicity, let me just stay with the Krajina Corps documents for now, as I've explained to Your Honour -- I've explained when they were disclosed, who we've received them from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've explained the purpose; to impeach.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I've explained the purpose. And, quite frankly, again, we didn't realise this would be so important until Wednesday afternoon, and that is why we're making this application now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any response, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understanding that all of these documents are being offered for the purpose of impeachment, and none other, I'm not sure that the conclusion that's been reached, which we didn't realise would be so important until Wednesday afternoon, meets the standard. Why is it so important? I think they have to say more than what their internal conclusion is here with regard to why these documents they believe are going to, in fact, operate to do that which I think they will do, which is impeach. So it's what we would call an offer of proof. To say it's important is meaningless. There's a reason behind the -- there's a reason why they believe they will impeach, using these documents, but perhaps we should hear what that reason is. Otherwise, all they're telling you is they think it's important, and that, in and of itself, doesn't meet any standards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I must admit, you are leaving me behind. I'm not with you. I don't know whether you are with him, Judge. Let me try and read what you have -- let me read what you have said. If I think I understand what you are saying, the reason is impeachment. Until Wednesday afternoon, they didn't know that the Defence was going to tender evidence that says that the Drina Plan was a camouflage. Now that they are aware that it has been tendered as -- it's been explained as a camouflage, they see the importance to dispute that. And that is the reason behind their application to want to tender these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, you explained it better than Mr. Saxon did. And with that as an understanding, then I have no further comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then if you have --what does that -- "I have no further comments," what does that mean in terms of their application to use the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To the extent the documents are solely being used for purposes of impeachment, then they would have met the threshold.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the Drina documents may be used, sir -- the 1st Krajina documents. I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, before we lose -- before we leave the topic of the 1st Krajina Corps documents, I have one more application to make. Again, the Prosecution chose not to put these documents on its 65 ter list, and so it chose, to save resources, not to translate them. All right? Wednesday afternoon, we see, as we've discussed already, the importance of the documents now to use them with this particular witness. We don't have them, obviously, in such a short period of time, in the English language. We're asking for the Chamber's patience and leave to allow me to review the key portions of these documents with the witness in his language. That's what I'm asking you to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, if I -- considering that they've had the documents since at least 2007, when they gave them -- supplied them to the Defence, I find it somewhat odd that they haven't been translated. But apart from that, it creates another problem here, which is: In the absence of -- in the absence of the documents being translated so the Chamber can look at them and so we are in a position to fully look at them with regard to any objections that may arise internally with regard to any document, we are disadvantaged. It would make sense for us to have the document so that we are in a position to address whatever issues may or may not come up. I don't know if any issues would come up or not, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The Defence have had the documents for three years, Your Honour, in the language of the excused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, you know what? I mean, at this point in time, this is -- this is an interesting conversation. Quite frankly, they've got the burden of proof. They chose not to introduce these documents. They chose not to call witnesses. We relied on that. We're entitled to rely on that, because the Prosecution has to prove their case. And if they choose not to call witnesses about a particular matter, and if they choose not to introduce documents about a particular matter, none of that in any way should enure to our detriment. And in no way should there be any responsibility that enures to us by virtue of the Prosecution's failure to present their case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, lead counsel for Mr. Perisic is fully equipped to read these documents and follow them, as is the witness, as is General Perisic. If it would assist the Defence, we can tender them marked for identification at a certain time and then seek the appropriate translations so then they can be reviewed and dealt with at a later time. I'm asking for leave to use them today, while the witness is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So if they do come in, they would be marked for identification precisely because they're not been translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I was -- if I may, just intervene on your intervention, Mr. Guy-Smith. You indicated that you would be disadvantaged, and Mr. Saxon has already referred to what I wanted to raise with you, that to the extent that at least on your side you have been able to understand B/C/S, to that extent are you even better advantaged than everybody else. However, I hear what Mr. Saxon says, when he says when they decided - and I don't know when that decision was taken - when they decided that they were not going to use these documents, they decided to save the resources of the Tribunal and not have them translated. Now they have now become important for them since Wednesday, the 24th of February this year. In that short period of time, they were not able to have them translated. The witness is here. We can do it in two ways. We can either use these documents, mark them for identification, have them translated later, and try to work as detailed as we possibly can while this witness is here, or we don't use these documents, but then this witness must come back once they're translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood. I'm getting a communication from my colleague here. If I could -- if I could do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And if you can switch off your microphone --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- to make sure that we don't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So the record is complete with regard to this issue: After speaking with my colleague, we received - XN-144 through 155 - notice that those documents would be used today, at 2.15 p.m. That is the first time we received notice that these particular documents would be used for purposes of cross-examination. Number 1, the reason that's of importance is we were supposed to receive, at the time the cross-examination starts, a list of those documents which are to be used. That was yesterday. Yesterday, we received, at 5.02 p.m., notice that 178 documents would be used. And those 178 documents did not include documents XN-144 through 155. So there's a problem already with regard to -- there's a guide-line problem here, in terms of the way things are supposed to occur. But be that as it may -- there are two other issues that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I suggest that you sit down while he's on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. But, of course, you know I'm not so good at sitting down, but I'll try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, unfortunately, the ethics of court is that while one counsel is on his feet, the other must sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Be that as it may, my understanding, from what Mr. Saxon has told us, is that documents that were not translated into English he became aware of as being important for purposes of examining this particular witness. I have a question, because unless I'm mistaken, Mr. Saxon is not conversant in B/C/S, so I'm not quite clear as to how he became aware of the importance of these documents in a language which he is not familiar with. However, be that as it may, in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Don't be impatient with me. I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the event -- I'm not being impatient with you, Your Honour. I'm having some -- never mind what I'm having. You really, quite frankly, don't want to be in my head right now, or maybe you do. Be that as it may, as I was saying, in the event that the Chamber finds that the late notice of these documents - and by that I mean the failure to include them on the initial list at the commencement of cross-examination - is to be permitted, I believe that we have a position. However, we would ask for a ruling with regard to that issue first, because otherwise what we're going to get into, I'm afraid of, and this is perhaps the first example of it, is as the cross-examination goes along, they go, Oh, well, here's some more documents that we'd like to use for purposes of cross-examining this individual that we never put on the 65 ter list but were available. And we're going to end up in a situation where there're going to just be bucket-loads of documents that come in during the lengthy process of their cross-examination, as opposed to a cogent determination at the commencement of their cross-examination that these are the documents that are going to be used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Guy-Smith is correct that when the Prosecution, yesterday afternoon, sent its list of documents to be used on cross-examination of General Simic, XN-144 through 155 were not included on the list. And that was due to an error which I will explain, an error that I discovered this morning. We've looked at today Prosecution Exhibit P1562, which is the list of documents from the 1st Krajina Corps. It was the Prosecution's misapprehension, beginning on Wednesday night, when it first began to look at this issue, that the documents that are XN-144 through 155 were part of P1562. I discovered, at about 10.00 this morning, that we were wrong, that they were part of the 65 ter material that eventually became P1562. We were wrong about that. As soon as I realised we were wrong, I called Mr. Lukic and explained the error, and we had the documents up-loaded as soon as we could. Your Honour, if we're going to be clashing over guide-lines, I could also point out, for example, that with respect to this witness, on Saturday of last weekend -- excuse me. On Friday, a week ago, the Defence deadline for providing its list of exhibits for this witness for direct examination was due to the Prosecution, two working days before the start of direct examination. On Saturday evening, the Defence sent the Prosecution a list of 27 additional documents that it would use -- potentially use as exhibits with this witness. Out of collegiality, I did not raise that with the Trial Chamber. I told Mr. Simic [sic] that. I'm surprised, quite frankly, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You told Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. It's late Friday afternoon. I told Mr. Lukic that I wouldn't, and I didn't. So I'm frankly that this -- I'm a bit surprised that this argument is being made, but there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The argument has been made. And as I understand the argument, it turns around the question of notice to the Defence and the question of fair trial. And if that is the feeling of the Defence about that point, which you concede, if this Chamber is going to be forced to make a ruling, and if the two of you don't agree, we're going to have to give the Defence adequate notice before we use those documents. You can decide, before we make a ruling, whether you want a postponement so that notice is given or whether you want to carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're not going to finish with the witness today. That is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So what I will do is I will not use these Krajina Corps documents today. I will save them until Monday to give the Defence the weekend to review them. And I hope that would clear up any potential unfairness to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you have other documents that you could use with the witness today?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: With the leave of the Chamber, absolutely, Your Honour. They are on our list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, let's find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I could have but a moment with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We appreciate Mr. Saxon's accommodation in this regard, and the weekend would be time sufficient for us to be able to grapple with those issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then that brings me, Your Honour, to another group of Drina Plan documents, and I believe I can say, in all truthfulness, that this group were put on the Prosecution's list to be used in cross-examination. They are the documents that were referred to as XN-132 and the documents that were referred to as XN-133. Let me start with what has been up-loaded onto e-court as XN-132. Your Honour, again this would fall within the category of fresh evidence. These are documents obtained from the Government of Republika Srpska by the Office of the Prosecutor, and they are documents from the Drina Corps, the Army of Republika Srpska, related to the Drina Plan. They were disclosed to the Defence on the 10th of August, 2007, via CD-ROM. And, again, the Prosecution seeks to use these documents with this witness, tender them for the purposes of impeachment, because they speak to the important issue first raised by the Defence, through this witness, on Wednesday afternoon; that is, that the Drina Plan was not a genuine document or a genuine plan. So we have 18 such documents from the Drina Corps, Your Honour. Also, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just hear me out. I thought you said it's XN-132 and XN-133, which gave me the impression it's two documents. Now you say 18 documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour is correct. They have been up-loaded into e-court under -- the Drina Corps documents have been up-loaded onto e-court under a single number, XN-132. But within XN-132, there are 18 such documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And any response from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe there's a translation issue with regard to these documents. We do not object to them being MFI'd, if they reach the point of being -- if they reach a point where they are being tendered as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Guy-Smith is correct. Just as with respect to the Krajina Corps documents that have not been translated into English, nor have the Drina Corps documents been translated. So if we're given permission to use them, I would also seek your leave to use them in the language of the accused for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And you said you don't object, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After consultation with my colleague, we do not object, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Well, then those documents, XN-132 and XN-133, called the Drina Plan documents, may be used, and they will be MFI'd, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if you'll let me clarify, because maybe I wasn't clear before. The documents that have been up-loaded under XN-133 are documents produced by the Sarajevo Romanija Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, not the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Not the Drina Corps. That's why they were given a different number on e-court. I'm sorry if I wasn't clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, we have a set of Drina Corps documents, that is, XN-132, and a set of Sarajevo Romanija Corps documents, XN-133. And from the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, we have six documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Saxon. You got that right? XN-132 are Drina Corps documents; XN-133 are Sarajevo Romanija documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's what I understand are the representations made by Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There are a total of 24 documents; 18 documents as relates to XN-132, 6 documents as relates to XN-133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that the issue -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe that those mathematics are correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Then both the Sarajevo Romanija Corps documents and the Drina Corps documents, numbered XN-132 and 133, respectively, may be used. They shall be MFI'd, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Shall we bring the witness back now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness may come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Once again, we are very sorry, Mr. Simic. These are the vicissitudes of trials. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Once again, good afternoon, Mr. Simic. I believe we may need to give the general a different binder. It would be the second Drina Plan binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General, if you could please take a look at what is tab 1, and this is part of the first document of XN-132.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We'll wait for it to come up on the screen so other people can follow along. I don't know if that can be rotated somehow. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, this appears to be the cover of a binder. Can you read for us, please -- we're going to go now into the realm of the Drina Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska. Can you read what that label says in the binder, please? Can you read it out loud?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, Drina Corps, and, "Drina."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. And just so you understand, General, this next series of documents, we don't have them translated into English, so I may rely on you a little bit more now to read some parts of things into the record. But we'll do this as efficiently as we can. If you turn to tab 2, please, in the binder. It should be the next document in XN-132.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have some concern with what Mr. Saxon just said, that he's going to use a witness to read things into the record. I don't think that's an appropriate use of the witness, to read things into the record, when he is using these documents for purposes of impeachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm surprised at that -- I'm surprised at that submission, because in the last series of documents, when we were discussing sanctions, the general read several pieces of documents into the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Undeniably so, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, what's your authority for that submission?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have no case law for that authority. However, I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: A rule or jurisprudence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: However, I believe that what is being done here, if it is for the purpose of impeachment, then what one does is they present the evidence for which they wish to impeach the witness to them and then engage in whatever appropriate questions they believe establish that impeachment. But to have him establish the record, which is what I'm referring to -- to have the witness establish the record is not an appropriate manner of dealing with documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The record --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- because the document, itself -- the document, itself, is that which is being relied upon, not him reading it into the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The record is the document, itself, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, with that in mind, then I have no difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I work with the document at tab 2, I neglected to tender the first document into evidence marked for identification. That was the first document under XN-132. It was the cover of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The cover?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yeah, and I'm asking if that could be given an exhibit number now, MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm advised that in that case, you'll have to re-upload it as a separate exhibit, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then what I will do is I will work with the witness and ask for the entire group of documents to be given an exhibit number, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The entire XN-132?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, if you could focus your attention on the document in tab 2, please. At the top, in the middle, it says: "Plan of intelligence security." Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. What does it say?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Plan of intelligence support for the performing of a defensive and offensive operation of the Army of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. On the left-hand side, we see a stamp of the VRS Main Staff. And are you able to see the signature of General Mladic on that stamp? Are you able to see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And then on the right side at the top, it says: "State Secret, Drina." Doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite. It says "People's Defence, State Secret, Drina."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And then it says, below that: "Attachment Number 5." And there's a --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There's a copy number, but I'm, quite frankly, having a hard time reading it. Do you see that? Perhaps it's a "4" or a "9."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It could also be a "7."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It might be, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To me it looks more like "Copy Number 7."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, if you go back to the left side of the top of the page, where we see the stamp and Mladic's signature, doesn't it say there that it's been approved by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see -- if we could go to the next page, please. We see, again, at the bottom of this chart, another seal of the VRS Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then, if we could turn to the last page, please. I'm sorry. I'm very, very sorry. I misspoke. I should have said "the next page" for e-court purposes. My mistake. E-court page 4. General, do you see on that page there's a signature by Colonel Petar Salapura? Do you see that, and a seal?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And he was the -- he was in charge of the Intelligence Sector for the Main Staff of the VRS; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the assistant of the commander of the Main Staff for intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could turn, General, to tab 3 in your binder, please, and if we could go to the next document in what is XN-132. It would be the next page, probably, in XN-132. Yes, it is. General Simic, can you read -- this particular document actually is a total of three pages. If we stick with the first page here, can you read the title of the document at the top?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I have turned to the right document, then it reads "Order for Intelligence Support."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in the upper right-hand corner, we see "People's Defence, State Secret, Drina," again, don't we?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then "Attachment Number 4" and "Copy Number 7." Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Completely, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At the bottom of the first page, we see the seal of the VRS Main Staff; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we turn to the next page, please. Again, at the bottom we see the seal of the VRS Main Staff. And then can we please go to the last page of this document, just the next page in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at the bottom, you'll see the seal of the VRS Main Staff, and signed by the commander, Ratko Mladic. Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can we turn -- General Simic, if you simply go now to tab 4 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could we go to the next page in XN-132.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, this is a plan for camouflage, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Plan of Operative Camouflage." The term "deception" has been used here, but it's called "Plan of Operative Camouflage" where I'm from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And so this would be a plan describing the different kinds of deceptive tactics that would be carried out; right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It provides measures of how certain deceitful actions are going to be taken or what documents should be planted to agents of foreign secret or intelligence services in order to deceive the enemy about our actual intentions. That was the purpose of what we call, in theory, camouflage. You can see here that it's "operative camouflage," but when I explained the directive, that had to do with strategic camouflage. You have camouflage at all levels of planning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And on the left-hand side, it says -- on the upper left-hand corner, we see a stamp. And, again, this has been approved by Ratko Mladic, hasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has been obscured by numbers and by the stamp. I think it's "Mladic," but I cannot read it clearly. However, since it says "I approve," it must have been the commander, Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you so much for that. Can you stay on that page for a moment and turn your eyes to the far right-hand side, at the top. And, again, we see "People's Defence, State Secret, Drina," don't we? Followed by an attachment number and a page number?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we scroll down in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On this last page, we see the seal of the VRS Main Staff, and then this -- it looks like it's been signed by Radivoje Miletic. Do you recall what his position was? Or "Miletic?"

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, in this document, "Head of the Administration for Operations and Training." That is the function of Mr. Miletic on the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, the same position that I had in the General Staff of the VJ. To put it briefly, he was an operative.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So this document would have been -- this plan would have been prepared by General Miletic for the approval of General Mladic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only Miletic, but the whole operations organ, just like I had my own administration on the General Staff, and I wasn't such a clever man like Bismark to do it all by myself. I had a whole group working on the preparation and drafting of the document. The fact that I signed it gives me the right to do so based on the order from the Chief of General Staff. Equally, Mr. Miletic received similar orders from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. So you raise an interesting point. So, for example, the production of these kinds of plans, they require the concerted efforts of a group of officers, don't they?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn to tab 5 in your binder, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, I believe - correct me if I'm wrong - this is a list of documents from the Main Staff of the VRS that was delivered to the Drina Corps. Is that a correct summation of what we see at the top here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. We see, on the upper left-hand corner, the date, "3 January 1994." And, again, on the right-hand side, "People's Defence, State Secret, Drina." I believe that would be copy number two. General, one copy of this document would have been kept by the Main Staff of the VRS; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you followed what I was talking about earlier, when I spoke about the Drina Plan at its strategic level, I said that plans were always drafted in two copies. One copy is always retained by those who elaborated the details. In this particular case, it was the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. And the second copy, in the form of an extract, which was important for the Command of the Drina Corps, was submitted to them. And this is the list of documents that they received at the Drina Corps. If you allow me one more sentence. The entire plan of the Main Staff of the VRS was not available to corps commanders. What they had was something that was specifically related to their tasks or possibly neighbouring units that possibly depend on the execution of their tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for that helpful clarification. Can you stay on this same page, General, but focus your eyes on the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we scroll down on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, you'll see that this list contained 15 items. You see that? It goes down to number 15?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at the bottom of that page, we see a date, "13 January 1994," and below that the seal of the VRS Main Staff. Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, please. Are you -- I believe on the next page, in the upper left-hand corner, it says "Documents Drina from the VRS Main Staff." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, please. And we see on this page it looks like a table, and in item 1 -- in item number 1, we see the date "9 January 1994." And then in the next column, this is a difficult word for me to pronounce, but does it say "Naredjenje"?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Naredjenje," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What does "Naredjenje" mean?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, in the list of documents, is entitled an order. So some order is being issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And then in item 2, in the first column, we see the date "3 January 1994." And then in the next column over, it says "List of documents." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then in the next column, we see the number "15." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that number 15 on this page confirms the receipt of the 15 documents on the list of the first page, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But under number 1, there's a covering letter that goes with this order. And this list is an integral part of the plan, whereas the covering letter contains his order to work these plans into more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I imagine an order like that would also require the concerted efforts of a number of officers to produce. Wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a very short order. All he's saying is that his subordinate must act in accordance with a plan and proceed with the elaboration of his own documents. Therefore, there was no need for any elaborate and cumbersome order. It just contained two or three sentences.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for correcting me. Can you turn to tab 6, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page in e-court. General, correct me if I'm wrong, like you just did, but it's my understanding that this is a document addressed to the Air Force and the Anti-Aircraft Defence about the preparation of a plan. Is that what it says in the first two lines of text at the top?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is this an order? The word below that in all capital letters, is that the word "ORDER"?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, in the army, use imperative mode. Therefore, this reads literally "I hereby order," which means that he issued an order to them to act in accordance with the extracts received that referred to the RV and PVO, meaning that they should prepare their own plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, on the right-hand side it says "Drina R, Copy Number 7."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we scroll to the bottom of this page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At the very bottom, to the left of the seal, we see some text, beginning with the word "Radjeno." Can you tell us what this text says or what it means?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that this order was made out in eight copies and submitted to the Archive, to the Command of the 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps, the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, the Eastern Bosnian Corps, and the other corps as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The other corps of the Army of Republika Srpska; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am talking all the time and you're asking me all the time about the documents that came from the Main Staff and the subordinate units of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. We see the seal of the Main Staff, the signature of General Milovanovic. Can you turn to tab 7, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we go to the next page in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you look at the first page with me now, General, please. You'll see, in the upper right-hand corner, it says "People's Defence, State Secret, Drina, Attachment 2, Copy Number 7." What is the title of this document, General? Or let me put the question to you directly: Is the title "Intelligence Situation"?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we scroll to the bottom of this page, we see the seal of the Main Staff. Can we turn the page, please. And we see, on the bottom of that page, the seal of the Main Staff. Can we go to the next page. Again, the seal of the Main Staff. And on until -- can we go to -- can we go ahead one or two more pages, please, and it should say "Page 8" at the top. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is page 21 in e-court. We see the seal on the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, very briefly, why would a report about the intelligence situation form a part of the Drina Plan?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how shall I put it? All other measures taken by the command derive from the prevailing intelligence situation in order for them to carry out their tasks. They are mainly talking about what the tasks of the aggressor would be, what the probable or possible mode of activities of the Croatian Army would be, what kind of operations would be launched by the Muslim forces, how the enemy forces are expected or anticipated to act; and this would enable the commander to figure out how to resist these actions. This is the purpose of intelligence reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you turn to the next tab in your binder. That's tab 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General, if you could just focus for now on the top of the first page. At the top of the first page, we see, in all capital letters, the word "INSTRUCTIONS." Instructions for what? You see it at the top of the first page, General Simic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, please give me some time to look at the document to enable me to give you an answer. You asked me about what an instruction means. In order for me to grasp that, I have to look at the content of the document to give you a valid answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Yugoslav Army, the word "instruction" is not commonplace when it had to do with the Drina Plan of use.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry. I'm very sorry to interrupt. I think perhaps my question was not clear. My question was: You see at the top of the first page the word "Instruction," but I can't read the text immediately below that word, so I can't -- I don't know - and I'd like you to help the Chamber - tell us, instructions regarding what particular unit or topic? Can you just tell us what it says there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Prosecutor. It reads literally as follows: "Instruction for executed command and co-ordinated action in anti-aircraft defence and air support."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see, on the upper left-hand corner, that this was approved by General Mladic. You see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Again, a reference to the Drina Plan on the upper right-hand corner. And could we please go - let's see - eight more pages forward, please. That's it. And it's a page, General, where we see the word "Prila [phoen]." If you look at the screen in front of you, we see the seal and a signature from an officer named Maric below the word "Prilok [phoen]." Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, no worries.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Who was Colonel Maric, if you know, or what position did he hold?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise answer to this question, and I'm reluctant to improvise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right, that's fine. But in this case, Colonel Maric would have prepared these instructions for the approval of General Mladic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please. Can you tell us in summary, briefly, what do we see on this page? It has ERN 0433-6601. I believe at the top it says something about signals. What does it say at the top?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reads: "A. Signals indicating danger - alerts." Under B, in the middle of the document, it says: "Signals of co-ordinated action and anti-aircraft defence." You asked me about this instruction before. I said that it is not commonplace, in this kind of plans, to use the word "instructions." We are talking about the plan for co-ordinated action, how the Air Force and Anti-Aircraft Defence is going to act in concert with the units that it provides support to. Now we have the word "co-ordinated action" here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a correction in the transcript. On page 86, line 21, the witness said "in our environment" or "with us." I would like the witness to explain what he meant.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant that in the documents produced by the General Staff of the VJ, this document would have been called a plan for co-ordinated action.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. I think Mr. Lukic could have done that in redirect examination, but that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was just a translation issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That wasn't clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, I'm sorry, very briefly, because we have to pause now, but my question, in particular, for this page is : What kind of information is on this page, is recorded here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under item A, "Signals for danger - alerts," it says air raids would be conveyed by telephone, like alert, or air-raid, or by radio communication 22-22. Next one, danger from --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that it is very difficult to translate, simultaneously, written documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I think we can stop now for the day. I think we've done enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry about that, Madam Interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We, unfortunately, are not done with you, so you're going to have to come back on Monday at quarter past 2.00 in Courtroom I. I warn you again, you may not discuss the case with anybody, and in particular not with your counsel. Court adjourns to Monday, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, in Courtroom I. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 1st day of March, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
